doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Coltrane, bebop and teaching jazz from John Coltrane onward
summary: He never cared for Coltrane, calls bebop an exclusionary language, and says those who start jazz history with Coltrane have no clue.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well I never really cared for his playing. I never cared for his sound. I can appreciate him more now than I could when he first came out. I just never — there was — like bebop, to me it was a language that was trying to cut guys like me off, or out of the picture. Whatever it was, it didn’t concern me. It was not my lingua franca. I would still hold that to be true today, that anybody trying to do that or play that kind of music who is not from that era or a descendent of that era of people, then they’re outsiders. Sorry.
There’s some people in jazz who teach it who feel like jazz started with John Coltrane.

Correct. Certainly. Those poor fools haven’t got a clue I’m sorry to say. I mean if you want to teach jazz you take it back to where it’s able to be taught from and when it’s the most understandable, when it was still part of the popular culture, where the kids, that was their music. They were the rebels. Their parents looked at that kind of music, oh that’s awful, dreadful, jazz music. Even Miles Davis’ parents, you know, didn’t condone jazz music because it was the devil’s music, it was this kind of music, it brought on sexual, whatever, fantasies come true, along with the forbidden weed. But I mean there are the tunes that I’m talking about, that the kids could identify with. The same kids with the same mentality today who are listening to the same — unfortunately not the same music but the same tribal energy that used to go up making sixteen men in a band perform like one, you’ve got four guys plugged into amplification and can fill up Yankee Stadium with this horrendous tribal music and cause the same kind of frantic thing that they did in 1938 or 1928. Same thing. Nothing has changed. Because if man learned from history he wouldn’t be repeating the same stupidity. They still do it though.
